subject: BAA applicability & delegated-processing details for PHI (Acme Health)
messages:
From: Sarah Lopez <sarah.lopez@acmehealth.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 15 Mar 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Inquiry: BAA applicability and delegated processing (Acme Health)

Hi Rishi,

Thanks for the product overview earlier. We're evaluating Redwood for a pilot that will route limited PHI (patient identifiers + visit notes) into an LLM-based summarization pipeline. Before we proceed with a PoC, legal and security have a few clarifying questions about where Redwood sits in the processing chain and whether you're able to sign a Business Associate Agreement (BAA). Specific asks below — can you confirm what applies and (ideally) send evidence where available: 

- Are you willing to sign a BAA for our use case? If so, does that cover hosted (shared) API, Dedicated instances, or only Private/VPC deployments?
- From a legal perspective do you consider Redwood a "Business Associate" (on-behalf processor) or a subprocessor acting under our control?
- Can you provide a short dataflow diagram showing what PHI is stored/transient, where KV cache and logs live, and how long telemetry/audit logs are retained?
- Evidence of encryption at rest and in transit (algorithms / KMS/HSM), and whether customer-managed keys are possible.
- Audit rights / right-to-audit clauses and available audit evidence (SOC 2 Type II, AOC, HIPAA control mappings).
- Do you persist prompt or response content for model improvement by default? If so, what opt-outs exist?

We can share a high-level architecture of our PoC if that helps you map controls. Legal would like an initial answer and a rough timeline for a formal BAA + countersigned template so procurement can plan.

Thanks — Sarah
Sarah Lopez
Head of Information Security
Acme Health

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: Sarah Lopez <sarah.lopez@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 15 Mar 2028 10:04:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Inquiry: BAA applicability and delegated processing (Acme Health)

Hi Sarah — great to hear from you and thanks for the clear list. Short answers up front, with attachments and a security handoff below: 

- We do sign BAAs, primarily for Dedicated and Private (VPC / on-prem) deployments; Hosted/shared API is generally limited to de-identified or non-PHI workloads unless we agree to an exception in contract.
- We function as a processor/business associate when handling PHI under a BAA for Dedicated/Private customers; for Hosted/shared customers we remain a service provider but will not sign a BAA by default.
- Attached is a one-page BAA summary (redwood_baa_summary_v1.pdf) and an example dataflow diagram (dataflow_acme_example.png).
- SOC 2 AOC (soc2_aoc_2027.pdf) is attached; will route any HIPAA-specific control mapping to our security team.

I'll loop in Priyom and Laura on next steps — they'd like to get a short call scheduled to walk through your PoC architecture, then we'll route to Security for a formal statement and a BAA template. Are you available tomorrow at 11:00am PT for a 30-minute call?

Best,
Rishi
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Attachments: redwood_baa_summary_v1.pdf (PDF), dataflow_acme_example.png (image), soc2_aoc_2027.pdf (PDF)

From: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
To: Sarah Lopez <sarah.lopez@acmehealth.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 15 Mar 2028 13:26:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Inquiry: BAA applicability and delegated processing (Acme Health)

Hi Sarah — Monica from Security here. Thanks for the clear set of questions — below is a concise technical/legal position and the evidence we can provide quickly. If you need deeper artifacts (control mapping spreadsheets, WAF/IDS configs, or full DPIA) we'll prepare those but we'll need a signed NDA/POC intake in place first.

Position (high level):
- BAA: Redwood will execute a BAA for customers housing PHI on Dedicated or Private deployments. For shared/hosted API we require de-identification or a documented exception approved by Legal and Security (rare).
- Role: Under a signed BAA we are a Business Associate / processor. We accept delegated processing obligations and will flow down controls to subprocessors (we maintain a subprocessors registry).

Technical controls / evidence we can provide immediately:
- Encryption: TLS 1.3 in transit; AES-256 at rest. Customer-managed KMS (bring-your-own-key) available for Private and Dedicated; hosted API can use encryption keys managed by Redwood. We support HSM-backed key wraps for high-sensitivity customers.
- Logging & retention: Audit logs retained by default for 90 days (configurable to 7 years for Dedicated/private customers per contract). Telemetry and model-improvement data ingestion is opt-in; default for PHI under a BAA is opt-out of model training.
- KV cache and ephemeral data: KV caches are ephemeral and isolated per customer on Dedicated/Private. For hosted API we do not persist KV cache beyond the request unless caching is explicitly enabled; see the attached diagram.
- Audit rights: We provide audit evidence (SOC 2 Type II AOC) and can support right-to-audit clauses with reasonable notice; for deeper audits (onsite or remote pentest/controls review) we'll coordinate through Legal and Security and scope via SOW.
- Controls mapping: We maintain a HIPAA control mapping aligned to our SOC 2 report; can share a mapping spreadsheet after an NDA.

Next steps we recommend:
1) Share a high-level PoC dataflow (redacted if needed) so we can confirm any data egress points.
2) Confirm desired deployment mode (Dedicated vs Private) and whether you need customer-managed keys.
3) Rishi / Laura to schedule the 30-min technical sync — we can bring the relevant infra engineer.

Quick notes on timeline: initial BAA template + SOC2 docs can be provided within 24 hours once we receive a signed mutual NDA (we can use a standard NDA). A countersigned BAA typically completes in ~1–2 weeks depending on legal review cycles.

Links/evidence: compliance package (https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2B3cREDWOOD-compliance-package), SOC2 AOC (attached).

Thanks — happy to jump on the call tomorrow if that works.

— Monica
Senior Security Engineer, Redwood Inference

Monica / Rishi — thanks, that's very helpful and addresses many questions. A few quick follow-ups: 

- We'll redact sample PHI for the PoC and share a simplified dataflow by end of day.
- We prefer Dedicated with BYOK (customer-managed keys). Please include any delta in cost/timeline for BYOK and extended log retention (7 years).
- Legal requests your standard BAA template and the SOC2 AOC PDF (we received the attachment). Please confirm whether Redwood's subprocessors list is current and the process for notifying us of new subprocessors.

We can take the 11:00am PT slot tomorrow for the technical sync — invite sent. Procurement will be looped for the BAA drafting.

Appreciate the quick turnaround.

Best,
Sarah

Acme Health
